description: How each normative statement in spec/ (a sentence with MUST or SHOULD) is tested. Ids are chapter:hash-of-sentence; check with `node tools/coverage.mjs`. Exactly one of vectors/schemas/examples (covered), elsewhere (covered by named engine or CLI tests), untestable, or gap (known, untested) per entry.

01:8ff5af41.text: ZIP entries MUST use UTF-8 names and MUST NOT contain absolute paths, `..` path segments, or duplicate names.
01:8ff5af41.note: duplicate entry names are rejected by csvx-go's unit tests; csvx-ts cannot create or read a duplicate entry (README, known gap)

01:c78b5fec.text: They MUST NOT be required for Core 1.0 packages.

01:8161243d.text: A sheet CSV MUST be valid UTF-8 RFC 4180-compatible CSV and MUST contain a header row.

01:f8c84e4c.text: A sheet entry MUST identify its CSV path and MAY identify its metadata sidecar.

01:5760d9ad.text: Readers MUST reject missing required entries, duplicate ZIP names, invalid UTF-8, and entries that exceed implementation resource limits.

01:7ffe5e46.text: Writers SHOULD use stable entry ordering and timestamps when producing reproducible archives.

01:b1e85b3e.text: The package MUST NOT require a proprietary binary format or a language-specific serialization format for its tabular data.
01:b1e85b3e.untestable: design principle: the format uses ZIP, CSV and JSON

02:9072d4f1.text: Sheet IDs and names MUST be unique within a workbook.

02:487c499c.text: `name` MUST start with a letter or `_`, continue with letters, digits, `_` or `.`, and MUST NOT look like a cell reference (`A1`, `$B$2`) or be `TRUE` or `FALSE`.

02:b983e257.text: Names are case-insensitive and MUST be unique within the workbook, ignoring case.

02:df2a911e.text: A name MUST NOT be a Core function name.

02:cf00f8f6.text: Every cell reference in it MUST be sheet-qualified, because a name has no home sheet.

02:edf62990.text: It MUST NOT itself use a name.

02:0ef37f35.text: A reader MUST reject it with the diagnostic code `INVALID_NAMED_RANGE`, naming the offending `name`.

03:8655c66f.text: The sidecar's `columns[].name`, when present, repeats that header text and MUST equal it.

03:0954dfe3.text: A reader MUST reject a sheet where they disagree, with the diagnostic code `COLUMN_NAME_MISMATCH`: silently picking one would hide an edit made to the other.

03:8c78ef2d.text: Quoting, commas, and newlines MUST follow RFC 4180-compatible CSV rules.

03:e154d4a0.text: It MUST NOT duplicate ordinary CSV values unless needed as a formula cache.
03:e154d4a0.gap: no vector checks that a sidecar does not duplicate CSV values

03:9f907aa1.text: Sheet names MUST be non-empty, no longer than 255 Unicode scalar values, and MUST NOT contain `:` or control characters.
03:9f907aa1.note: the empty-name case is covered for rename-sheet; the CSV import `name` option has no empty-string vector because Go treats an empty option as unset

03:a9e25628.text: Sheet IDs MUST be stable and MUST match the package resource names.
03:a9e25628.gap: no vector checks that sheet IDs are stable and match resource names

03:072b50c3.text: A renderer converts to pixels with `pixels = round(width * 7 + 5)` (the standard Calibri-11 approximation) and back with `width = (pixels - 5) / 7` when writing a pixel-based resize back to this field; neither direction is exact (real glyph widths vary slightly by character and by font), but both engines MUST use this same formula so a width written by one tool round-trips predictably through another.

03:e7646448.text: An interactive editor SHOULD present every sheet, including a newly created one, as at least the grid `A1:Z100` (columns A–Z, rows 1–100), padding the view with blank cells beyond the sheet's actual data.
03:e7646448.untestable: an interactive-editor presentation default; there is nothing for an engine to compute

03:17d46608.text: An engine MUST NOT pad or trim a sheet on load or save, and `create` and CSV import keep the extent of the source data.

03:685b5222.text: Settings are part of the workbook: an editor MUST write the print settings the user chose back to the sidecar, and a reader MUST preserve ones it does not understand.

03:8dc5c858.text: An engine MUST implement pagination exactly as follows, so every engine and renderer agrees on which cells land on which page.

04:d5d9ea47.text: All values MUST use an object with a `type` member.

04:28b394e2.text: `error` MUST use a stable `code` member and MAY include a diagnostic `message`; messages are not used for semantic comparison.

04:7e7b479a.text: Decimals MUST be encoded as base-10 strings.

04:cbe5aa00.text: Implementations MUST NOT silently convert invalid values to string.

04:c0315b82.text: A decimal's text is preserved exactly (`19.50` stays `"19.50"`); engines MUST NOT normalize it.

05:de43a3af.text: A formula cell MUST contain `formula`; it MAY contain a `cached` value produced by the last successful calculation.

05:04660707.text: Readers that calculate MUST replace it when the formula is evaluated.

05:0a94a7e8.text: Readers that cannot calculate MUST preserve the formula and cache byte-for-byte where practical.

05:ccd2c1d9.text: `type`, `formula`, and `cached` all describe a cell's current *content*, not the cell as a slot — an editor that replaces a cell's content (a new literal value, or one formula replacing another) MUST drop any `type` and `cached` that described the old content, the same way it MUST drop a stale `formula`.

05:858133a1.text: A reader with no declared type at all for a cell (no column type, no `type` override) MUST resolve its CSV text using the same literal rules as an untyped CSV value (see 04-data-types.md): blank, boolean, integer, or decimal by literal shape, otherwise string.

05:9ee35e3e.text: An editor that offers case conversion MUST use these rules, so every engine and app agrees on the result.

05:82e121b8.text: Formula cells and cells resolving to any other type, including `blank`, MUST be left exactly as they are:

05:f3d6ef50.text: A code point whose mapping is not exactly one code point (`ß` → `SS`, `İ` → `i̇`) MUST be left unchanged, which keeps the result identical in every implementation.

06:5e887df9.text: References are case-insensitive for matching but MUST retain their original spelling when preserved.

06:ae198055.text: Formula parsing MUST be deterministic and MUST reject trailing tokens, invalid references, and unsupported syntax.

06:1d952f3b.text: It MUST be accepted by the parser and preserved in the stored formula text.

06:f5134f0d.text: It is the spelling an engine writes into a formula when an edit destroys the cell a reference pointed to — for example deleting a row or column that the reference named — and the engine MUST preserve it in the stored formula text.

06:6bd84e82.text: A formula containing `#REF!` is syntactically valid: a parser MUST NOT report `NAME` or any other parse error for it.

07:f3b9e959.text: A function MUST return the same result for the same workbook state and MUST document its treatment of blanks, strings, dates, and errors.

07:f6304f1c.text: Unknown functions produce `NAME`; implementations MAY support extensions under a registered namespace, but MUST NOT reinterpret a Core function.

08:ba69c63d.text: Unsupported style properties MUST be preserved when round-tripping.

08:a602cf35.text: Number formats MUST NOT alter the underlying value.

08:450a089f.untestable: a writer preference; both forms are valid and read the same

08:3eb55247.text: Border color MUST NOT be rendered as an inset outline, box-shadow, or any other effect that draws inside the cell's content area: printing and export depend on the border sitting on the cell edge.
08:3eb55247.untestable: a rendering rule for renderers, not engines

09:2966212b.text: It MUST NOT change calculation semantics.

09:876f8c73.text: Invalid input SHOULD be reported with a stable machine-readable code and MAY be rejected by an interactive editor.

09:d4f6d3a3.text: A headless reader MUST preserve invalid values rather than deleting them.

10:db0e7f48.text: Independent cells MUST produce the same results regardless of worker scheduling.

11:c70d296d.text: They MUST NOT silently discard formulas, errors, styles, or unsupported metadata.

11:0025d1f5.text: Lossy conversions MUST report warnings with a location and reason.

11:ec74782a.text: A plain `.csv` file MUST be convertible to a CSVX workbook by every conforming engine and by `csvx-cli`.

11:e429f19e.text: Input that is not valid UTF-8 MUST be rejected, not transcoded by guessing.

11:b87ebe49.text: Input with no records at all (zero bytes, or only a byte-order mark and blank lines) MUST be rejected: a sheet needs a header row.

11:e8f23c4c.text: A `name` option that is empty, longer than 255 Unicode scalar values, or contains `:` or a control character MUST be rejected (`03-sheets.md`).

11:afb371a8.text: A field beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` is **not** a formula and MUST NOT gain a `formula` entry; it is a `string` (or a number if it matches a literal form, e.g.

11:3328ebb4.text: The importer MUST NOT strip, escape, or alter such a field (CSV-injection mitigation is a concern of whoever later exports to a spreadsheet application, not of import fidelity).

11:f9b44492.text: Malformed CSV (an unterminated quote, a stray quote inside an unquoted field) MUST be rejected with an error carrying the line number; importers MUST NOT repair it silently.

11:860eb2ac.text: `csvx-cli import` accepts a `.csv` input and writes a `.csvx` (it MUST map each option above to a flag and print warnings to stderr).
11:860eb2ac.elsewhere: csvx-cli end-to-end tests drive `csvx import` on CSV input with each flag and check stderr

11:44a6a7be.text: Engines MUST NOT add options or defaults beyond this list without amending this document.
11:44a6a7be.untestable: a process rule about amending the document

11:5ab8ea16.text: The extension SHOULD be implemented early enough to validate CSVX against real XLSX workbooks; it MUST provide exact-source recovery for unchanged embedded sources and explicit diagnostics for regenerated exports.
11:5ab8ea16.elsewhere: csvx-go Convert tests and csvx-cli end-to-end tests recover an unmodified embedded source byte for byte

12:bf709b4d.text: CSVX readers MUST treat workbook content as untrusted data.
12:bf709b4d.untestable: a principle; the specific obligations are the statements that follow

12:6cba6365.text: They MUST NOT execute macros, scripts, external links, formulas with side effects, or embedded files automatically.
12:6cba6365.gap: no vector shows that loading never executes anything; engines simply have no execution path

12:ae67eea6.text: Readers SHOULD enforce configurable limits for archive size, compression ratio, entry count, JSON depth, cell count, formula length, and formula dependency count.
12:ae67eea6.gap: neither engine has configurable limits yet, so there is nothing to test

12:218c98b2.text: ZIP extraction MUST defend against path traversal and resource exhaustion.
12:218c98b2.elsewhere: engine unit tests reject absolute, `..` and NUL entry paths; no vector

12:05f547c9.text: A conforming Core implementation MUST reject or quarantine them, not fetch them.
12:05f547c9.gap: external references are not loaded by either engine, but no vector asserts rejection

12:b706a7d8.text: Error messages SHOULD avoid exposing local filesystem paths or secrets.

13:13884d65.text: Test comparisons MUST be semantic for JSON object key ordering and exact for decimal strings, error codes, formulas, and coordinates.
13:13884d65.elsewhere: every engine runner compares semantically; this describes the runners themselves

13:25636635.text: A test runner SHOULD report implementation name, version, supported extensions, and each vector ID.
13:25636635.gap: no runner reports implementation name, version and vector IDs yet

14:8522fd83.text: XLSX behavior MUST NOT redefine Core values, formulas, calculation, or errors.

14:7ce34bfc.text: `source/original.xlsx` MUST be an opaque copy of the source bytes.
14:7ce34bfc.elsewhere: csvx-go tests check the embedded original is a byte-for-byte copy

14:7d199fcc.note: the source object is in workbook.json (and mirrored to source/source.json); every XLSX import vector validates its package against the schema

14:b4317637.text: The source hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of the embedded source bytes.
14:b4317637.elsewhere: csvx-go computes and verifies the SHA-256 in its XLSX tests

14:2c04fc8a.text: A reader MUST verify this hash before offering exact-source recovery.
14:2c04fc8a.elsewhere: csvx-go TestExportRefusesACorruptedEmbeddedSource flips one byte of an embedded source and expects the export to fail its SHA-256 check

14:2d7f3045.text: When `authority` is `original` and the CSVX workbook has not been modified, an exporter SHOULD return the embedded source bytes unchanged.
14:2d7f3045.elsewhere: csvx-go TestExportOfEditedPackageDoesNotReturnTheStaleOriginal and csvx-cli e2e recover an unmodified source

14:573963a2.text: After a supported CSVX edit, `authority` MUST become `csvx`.

14:0329b317.text: The exporter MUST NOT silently return an unchanged embedded source when that would hide the edit.
14:0329b317.elsewhere: csvx-go and csvx-cli end-to-end tests export an edited package and check the edit is present

14:7d1df5a2.text: An importer MUST inventory features it detects, including sheets, dimensions, values, formulas, cached results, shared strings, styles, number formats, merged cells, hidden content, validations, names, relationships, drawings, comments, images, charts, macros, and external references where applicable.
14:7d1df5a2.gap: the feature inventory has no vector

14:633ac029.text: Unsupported or lossy features MUST produce diagnostics with a feature category, source location when known, severity, and reason.

14:eb0c0413.text: An importer MUST preserve unsupported source resources when possible or report that they cannot be preserved.
14:eb0c0413.gap: preserving or reporting unsupported source resources has no vector

14:858dedc8.text: Implementations MUST treat embedded sources as untrusted data and MUST NOT execute macros or external links during import or export.
14:858dedc8.untestable: engines have no execution path for macros or links

14:c25347a9.text: Macro preservation and removal MUST be explicit policy decisions and MUST be reported in diagnostics.
14:c25347a9.gap: macro policy and its diagnostics are not implemented or tested

14:d3b735d4.text: An importer MUST map these XLSX constructs onto the sheet `print` object (03-sheets.md) and an exporter MUST map them back:

14:d9c8fc04.text: An importer SHOULD omit `margins` that equal the defaults in 03-sheets.md and `scale` of 100, since nearly every XLSX file states them and they carry no information.

14:a7971420.text: A paper size with no CSVX equivalent is not mapped to `paperSize`; the importer MUST keep the source value on the `print` object as `xlsxPaperSize` so it round-trips.

14:885ef045.text: An importer MUST therefore write worksheet row 1 as the CSV header row and worksheet rows 2 and later as data records.
14:885ef045.section: 14.7 Worksheet rows and the CSV header

14:4c71cdd6.text: An importer MUST map a workbook-scoped XLSX defined name (a `definedName` with no `localSheetId`) onto `namedRanges` (02-workbook.md) when its formula is a single cell reference, a single range, or a constant (number, string, or boolean), and its name satisfies the rules in 02-workbook.md.

14:0f7d4070.text: Every other defined name is not imported, and the importer MUST report each as a warning with the feature `definedName` and a message naming it and giving the reason: sheet-scoped, a formula that is not a single reference or constant (for example `OFFSET(...)`), a name that breaks the 02-workbook.md rules, or a built-in `_xlnm.` name with no CSVX equivalent.

14:80c5d5b1.text: If `authority` is `original` and the workbook is unmodified, an exporter SHOULD return the embedded source bytes instead.
14:80c5d5b1.elsewhere: same as 14.2: csvx-go and csvx-cli recover an unmodified source

14:6a32a7ed.text: An exporter MUST replace each forbidden character with `_`, shorten to 31 characters, make names unique ignoring case, rewrite every reference to the sheet in formulas and names, and report a warning for each change.

14:955c7e45.text: **Reporting.** An exporter MUST report each loss or transformation as a warning with feature, location and reason.

15:26822da4.text: An engine that edits a workbook MUST implement the operations in this chapter exactly as written, so that the same edit produces the same package in every engine and app.

15:d598a9a9.text: A consumer app MUST call the engine for them and MUST NOT carry its own copy (AGENTS.md §5).
15:d598a9a9.untestable: a rule for consumer apps (AGENTS.md section 5), not for engines

15:2d97b6da.text: An operation that is invalid (below) MUST fail without changing the workbook.

15:61e719f4.text: `at` MUST be ≥ 2, so the header row is never displaced;

15:e496591b.text: `delete-rows(sheet, rows)` deletes the given set of rows (duplicates ignored); every row MUST be ≥ 2 and exist.

15:3314e89c.text: `delete-columns(sheet, columns)` deletes the given set of columns; a sheet MUST keep at least one column.

15:1fe891b1.text: A workbook MUST keep at least one sheet.

15:cc210164.text: Properties the patch does not mention, including ones the engine does not understand, MUST be preserved (08-styles.md).

15:aad0ed64.text: The result MUST conform to the sheet metadata schema, but the engine does not check that itself: schema validation is the canonical validator's job (AGENTS.md §3.3), so a saved package with a bad value is rejected there.
15:aad0ed64.untestable: states that the engine does not validate the schema; nothing to test

03:f4c270a7.text: A writer MUST write the sidecar, and reference it from `workbook.json`, whenever the sheet has anything to put in it (column types or widths, row heights, cell metadata, or print settings), so that none of it is lost and no reference points at a file that is not there.

11:a2a92022.text: An engine MUST be able to export any sheet of a workbook as a CSV file, and `csvx-cli export` MUST do so when its output has a `.csv` extension.
11:a2a92022.note: csvx-cli export is covered by its end-to-end tests (cli_e2e_export_csv_test.go) against these same vectors

11:11840d87.text: Engines MUST expose all five and MUST NOT add options or defaults beyond this list without amending this document.

11:deb5db75.text: An unknown sheet MUST be rejected. |

11:a8dafb71.text: No other field is quoted, and field content, including leading and trailing whitespace, leading zeros, and a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@`, MUST be written exactly: export neither escapes nor alters text (neutralizing formula injection is the concern of whoever opens the file in a spreadsheet application).

11:da441e12.text: A field is the cell's CSV text as stored, except that a formula cell is written from its value, which an exporter MUST obtain by recalculating the workbook first (10-calculation.md), so a stale or missing cache never reaches the file.

11:3e980b7c.text: CSV carries data only, so an exporter MUST report what it leaves out, as warnings with a feature and a location.

11:ff323b33.text: For a CSV in the canonical form above (LF, minimal quoting, rectangular, with a non-empty header), importing it with the default options and exporting the sheet with the default options MUST return the same bytes.

03:81c0262e.text: A reader MUST NOT require names to be non-empty, and a writer MUST NOT invent a name for a column that has none; an editor shows its own placeholder for a blank name, and the file keeps the truth.

11:4ba69d36.text: The CSV resource is written with LF terminators and minimal quoting, except that a record consisting of exactly one empty field is written as `""` (a bare empty line is not a record: readers skip blank lines, and a `""` line is read as that one empty field); field *content*, including embedded newlines, leading/trailing whitespace, and leading zeros, MUST be preserved exactly.

11:e4a31ba6.text: When `header` is `false` the importer MUST synthesize a header row in which every column has the empty name, and insert it as row 1, so the source's first record becomes row 2; it MUST report a warning saying data rows were shifted by one.

11:7b63516c.text: Each of these MUST be reported as a warning with the 1-based source record number (the header, when present, is record 1).

02:13eb6b75.text: Names MUST also be unique ignoring ASCII case, so `Sales` and `SALES` cannot both exist: formulas find a sheet by name (06-formulas.md, Sheet references).

06:27b8fd50.text: A parser MUST accept a quoted qualifier whether or not it needed quoting.

06:cbe07857.text: A writer that composes a qualifier (rename-sheet, 15-edit-operations.md; an importer, 14-xlsx-interoperability.md) MUST write it bare only when it is a valid bare qualifier, is not cell-like (letters followed by digits, such as `Q1` or `FY2026`, optionally with `$`), and is not `TRUE` or `FALSE` ignoring case; otherwise it MUST quote it.

06:0a4cea39.text: A range whose ends name different sheets (`Sales!B2:Other!B10`) is a three-dimensional range, which Core 1.0 does not have, and a range whose first end is unqualified but whose second is qualified (`B2:Sales!B10`) is ambiguous; a parser MUST reject both as invalid syntax.

10:4af4a464.text: Implementations MUST invalidate stale caches when dependencies change, on any sheet: a change to a cell recalculates every formula cell that depends on it directly or through other formulas, in every sheet of the workbook, not only the sheet that was edited.

10:0f2089c2.text: Implementations SHOULD expose the calculation timestamp separately from workbook content.
10:0f2089c2.untestable: a SHOULD about how an API exposes the calculation timestamp; no format-neutral observable

14:e5deb17a.text: An importer MUST write each qualifier as 06-formulas.md requires of a writer, so a name XLSX quoted needlessly is bare again, and an exporter writes the qualifier as XLSX accepts it, quoting any name that is not a plain identifier.
14:e5deb17a.gap: no XLSX fixture with a three-dimensional or external-workbook reference yet, and neither importer emits the warning

14:0c163541.text: An importer MUST NOT guess a meaning for either.
14:0c163541.gap: no XLSX fixture with a three-dimensional or external-workbook reference yet, and neither importer emits the warning

14:6f1506ed.text: It MUST report a warning with the feature `formula`, the cell's location, and the reason, and it MUST keep the cell's cached result as the cell's value without the formula, so no formula that Core would reject is written into the package.
14:6f1506ed.gap: no XLSX fixture with a three-dimensional or external-workbook reference yet, and neither importer emits the warning

15:f2e0117a.text: The name MUST satisfy 03-sheets.md and be unique in the workbook ignoring ASCII case (02-workbook.md), otherwise the operation is invalid; changing only the case of the sheet's own name is valid.

15:794f0862.text: The workbook MUST be recalculated afterwards (10-calculation.md), since formulas on other sheets may read the changed cell.

08:c14b28d1.text: An absent key takes its default; a writer SHOULD omit a key that equals its default.
08:c14b28d1.gap: no vector checks that a writer omits default-valued font keys; the engines write what they are given

08:0aafe715.text: Unknown keys in `font` MUST be preserved (above).

08:0e744fdf.text: Whether an editor grows a row to fit a larger font is its own behavior; an editor that does so SHOULD write the resulting height to `rowHeights` so the file, not the editor, holds it.
08:0e744fdf.untestable: a SHOULD on editor behavior; the stored rowHeights it asks for is covered by the row-height vectors, the auto-fit decision is UI-only

unmappedVectors.tests/calculations/named-ranges.json: covers how names evaluate (06-formulas.md, Names), which is stated without MUST or SHOULD and so is not a tracked requirement
unmappedVectors.tests/interop/xlsx-borders.json: covers the XLSX border mapping (08-styles.md, Borders), which is descriptive rather than MUST or SHOULD
